title: FOOTBALL | Ethan Pulliam Press Conference - 11/22/26
text: Ethan, one thing with with kids who grow up in Starkville is they don't really experience the Egg Bowl rivalry as much as kids who grew up in like Jackson or or the places where there's a lot of Old Miss uh fans. What was your experience with the Egg Bowl rivalry before you got to Mississippi State? >> I think growing up it just put me in a I guess I would say a better perspective uh of how it's one of the best rivalries uh like in the nation. I would say it's it's the best. Um, and just growing up and being around it as a kid, it it's it shaped and formed me uh to I who I am today. >> I know you want to always help your team, but uh yesterday just the one official punt, I mean, when you look at that aspect of it, offense stayed on the field and and maybe Kyle's going out there instead of you. How do you kind of handle that, but also kind of stay ready when it is your opportunity? just being able to be uh I guess I can call it you know being savvy being able to uh like as coach Leb say make the layups I look at that as a layup in the moment you know it's kind of hard to react in that time of that you know that millisecond of going on the ground and you know taking the penalty for the team because at the end of the day it's trying to put my team in the best position possible and you know taking that over whatever the punt result would have been uh just taking a chance and being able to put my team in a better position and getting that 5-yard penalty, getting us closer to trying to get the first down and possibly us getting the first down and and Kyle being able to kick a field goal later in that drive. Um that's the way I just kind of look at it is just being able to play the next play and asking myself how can I put myself in the best situation possible to help team win. >> Ethan, I know you started, you know, putting a little bit last year. This year you've you've you know been out there full time. just talk about your progress uh from year to year, how help last year helped you this year, and how you felt like you've come along. >> I think last year helped me uh in a big way of being able to uh I guess get it get it get this train rolling, I would say. um finding out areas where I'm strong in, finding out areas where I'm weak in, and taking that after last season going into the summer and working on it as a whole um all together, trying to put the pieces together and knowing that this year is going to be a different year, you know, with the task being able to handle it all um whether it's flipping the field if we're on our own territory or being able to pin them deep when we're around the 50. And [snorts] um I think this year I've really been challenged with you know pinning them deep for the most part is I found myself we have a lot of punts on our own 50 yard line or even on our own um 45. So just being able to control that and not you know limit touchbacks and that's the big thing is trying to see if I can put them inside the 10 yard line. >> Coach Levy was just praising you for how you've responded to some tougher moments early in the season and are punting the ball pretty well now. just what adjustments at all did you make in the last month or two or was it kind of just staying the course? >> Just stay in the course and trust in the process and you know the easiest thing would have been to go back and reshape you know mechanics and you know not be able to I guess I would say um you know overthink that was the biggest thing was you know overthinking a lot of the challenges. Uh, I think it was just keeping my head down and working and like going outside and doing drill work really helped because being out there. I would [snorts] say adjusting to the wind um is a big is the biggest factor. and just being able to go out there and visualize the field on some afternoons when we're done in practice. I'll catch myself out there at 2:00 and I'll walk the field every afternoon just trying to figure out, you know, what would I hit in this situation and if the wind's blowing this way? Um, you know, how would this affect my drop or I would say my my aiming point down the field. So, I feel like I've handled it really really well and it's it's been a great I'll say four or five weeks. Coach just said y'all be leaving for Tupelo on Thursday. Just talk about your plans for Thanksgiving with your family and what what that's going to look like. >> Uh I would say so we leave Thursday and obviously Thanksgiving's on Thursday. Uh they'll end up feeding us here for Thanksgiving meal. Um I'll be missing my grandma's cooking uh as she as she cooks every year. I been able to be a part of the family tradition every year. But, um, you know, just going to handle business first and being able to to know that my food will be back here when I get back after we win the game. >> Ethan, forgive me if you've been asked this question in the past, but obviously growing up in Starkville, I'm sure you've had the opportunity to go to some previous Egg Bowls in the past. Do you have any any, you know, childhood memories or anything about going to these egg bowls and, you know, feeling it before you actually started playing in it? I think one in particular, I think we all remember this one, uh, Elijah Moore hitting the celebration after the touchdown. I was there for that game and I just remember everybody on the edge of their seats during that whole fourth quarter u with them going and score the touchdown and [snorts] then us getting the ball back. Um, but the penalty ended up costing the game. I just remember being there for that moment and it was pretty fun. It was pretty fun. Yeah. >> Yep. Thank y'all.
